text: Oil jumps over $3 on Nov. 5 after new tanker attacks. Oil prices are in the news after Brent crude settled up $3.67 on Thursday, Nov. 5, following new attacks on tankers. The move came a day after both benchmarks fell more than 8% when the Democrats won control of Congress in the Tuesday midterm elections.. The price of oil has swung sharply as the war between the United States, Israel and Iran continues. The conflict began in February, when President Donald Trump launched strikes along with Israel. The war pushed fuel prices higher, and high fuel costs became a major concern for voters in the midterm elections. Attacks on oil tankers in the Gulf have continued at a fast pace. UK maritime security monitors said at least five vessels had reported incidents since Sunday, and October saw 35 vessels hit. Analysts are split on what comes next. Some expect renewed US military action against Iran, while others see room for diplomacy after the midterms. Iran has reportedly sent the U.S. A nuclear proposal through Qatar, but it will be discussed only after Washington meets what Tehran calls "seven demands."

What is Oil Prices? Brent at $98.29 a barrel on Nov. 5, 2026. Oil prices are the per-barrel cost of crude oil, quoted through benchmark futures contracts such as Brent and West Texas Intermediate (WTI). On Nov. 5, 2026, Brent settled at $98.29 a barrel, up $3.67, while WTI closed at $90.52. The figures move daily as traders react to the Iran war and shipping attacks in the Gulf.. Brent crude rose more than $3 on Nov. 5, 2026, after new tanker attacks in the Gulf, reversing a sharp fall the day before. Oil has swung widely since the US, Israel and Iran went to war in February, and fuel costs became a major issue in the midterm elections.. Brent rose 3.88% on Thursday, Nov. 5, after new strikes on tankers raised concern about supply. The day before, both benchmarks had fallen more than 8%, reaching their lowest closing levels since Aug. 31. Analysts described the rebound as caution that shipping would not return to normal quickly, even if diplomacy advanced. Attacks on tankers in the Gulf are running close to a record pace. The UK Maritime Trade Operations agency counted at least five vessels reporting incidents since Sunday, Nov. 1. October saw 35 vessels hit, the highest monthly total of the conflict. Iran's Revolutionary Guard said two tankers and a tugboat caught fire in separate incidents after attempting to use unauthorized routes through the Strait of Hormuz. Forecasts differ sharply. Rapidan Energy's Bob McNally put the chance of renewed US military action at 80% and expects both benchmarks to top $100. Eurasia Group, by contrast, lowered its odds of renewed US strikes to 60% and its odds of a deal to 10%. Iran has reportedly proposed a nuclear deal through Qatar, but only after Washington meets what Tehran calls "seven demands," including ending the naval blockade of Iranian ports.

What is a cold front and how does it bring cooler weather: Boston, Friday rain. A cold front is the boundary where a mass of cooler, denser air pushes under warmer air and forces it upward. As the cooler air moves in, temperatures drop, winds often shift, and rain or showers often form along the line before it passes.. WCVB forecast rain in Boston on Friday followed by a cooler weekend, and WHDH tied that Friday rain to a cold front bringing colder air for the weekend.. In Boston, a cold front is tied to the rain forecast for Friday. A heavy stripe of rain on that front, with the front bringing colder air into the weekend. Friday's highs were expected near 70°F, about 15° above normal, and by the weekend temperatures were expected to settle to levels more typical of early November. WCVB forecast a StormTeam 5 Weather Alert day for rain on Friday, followed by a few showers on Saturday and an isolated morning shower on Sunday. Highs were expected to return to near normal by Veterans Day on Wednesday. On a weather map, a cold front is drawn as a line with triangles on the side the cold air is moving toward. The rain often forms along the front ahead of it.

What is Brent crude?. Brent crude is a grade of crude oil that is extracted from the North Sea. Its price serves as a worldwide benchmark for oil. In the latest session, Brent settled at $116.72 a barrel, its highest settle since April.. The Dow fell more than 600 points on Friday as oil topped $100 a barrel, and Brent closed at its highest level since April. Renewed concern over the U.S.-Iran conflict drove the rise.. Brent crude is a type of crude oil, the unrefined petroleum that is turned into fuels such as gasoline and diesel. It is named for a North Sea oilfield and is traded in futures markets. Because many oil-producing countries sell their crude at prices tied to Brent, its price is widely watched as a global reference point. Traders also follow the West Texas Intermediate grade, the main U.S. Benchmark, which trades at a different price. Brent is quoted in U.S. Dollars per barrel. A barrel is a unit of 42 U.S. Gallons. Futures contracts let buyers and sellers agree on a price today for oil delivered later. Prices move with supply, demand, and worries about conflict or disruption in oil-producing regions. On Friday, Brent rose 3.1 percent to end at $116.72. West Texas Intermediate settled at $103.27 a barrel, up 3.8 percent. The increase followed reports that the United States and Israel might be preparing renewed strikes on Iran, part of a regional war that began in late February. Traders feared the U.S.-Iran conflict could flare up again. The rise in oil added to pressure on stocks that day, when the Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 1.23 percent, to 52,215.16, and the S&P 500 slipped 0.52 percent. Higher fuel costs also weighed on some businesses, such as discount retailers, whose profits are sensitive to diesel prices.
